input: Create a grocery list template I can reuse weekly

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing which food categories to include (produce, dairy, meat, pantry staples, etc.) determines the structure and completeness of the template.
The household size and who it is for (single person, family with kids, couple) directly affects quantities, categories, and item variety in the template.
Where the user shops (one store vs. multiple stores) affects whether the template needs sections organized by store or by aisle layout.
The format and tool (paper printout, Google Sheets, Notion, a notes app) completely changes how the template is built and shared.
Whether the user wants pre-filled staple items or blank category buckets changes how much structure is pre-loaded into the template.
Dietary restrictions or eating style (vegetarian, gluten-free, specific cuisine) determine which items and categories are relevant or should be excluded.
Understanding what would make this template feel truly useful — speed, completeness, flexibility — helps prioritize the right features.

gold.taskTitle: Build a reusable weekly grocery list template
gold.taskDescription: Create a structured grocery list template the user can reuse each week for their shopping.

questions.title: Which food categories must the template cover?
questions.description: Identify the sections to include, such as produce, dairy, meat, frozen, pantry, snacks, beverages, or household items.

questions.title: How many people are you shopping for?
questions.description: Determine household size and composition (e.g., single adult, couple, family with children) to tailor quantities and item variety.

questions.title: Do you shop at one store or multiple stores?
questions.description: Establish whether the template needs a single unified list or separate sections organized by different stores.

questions.title: What format or app should the template live in?
questions.description: Decide on the tool — printed sheet, Google Sheets, Notion, Apple Notes, a grocery app, etc. — so the template is built in the right medium.

questions.title: Should staple items be pre-filled or left blank?
questions.description: Determine whether the template ships with common recurring items already listed, or provides empty category buckets for the user to fill each week.

questions.title: Are there any dietary restrictions or eating styles to reflect?
questions.description: Capture constraints like vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, halal, or a specific cuisine focus that should shape which items are included or excluded.

questions.title: What would make this template feel genuinely useful each week?
questions.description: Understand the user's top priority — e.g., speed of use, never forgetting items, tracking budget, or easy editing — to emphasize the right features.
